newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello say Australian rates low.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello say Australian rates low.

text.p: Australian interest rates are historically low and past cuts have yet to have an impact on the economy, Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday.

Asked by a television interviewer about the prospect of further monetary easings, Costello said: "Interest rates are very low by historical standards in Australia but they still have to work their way into the system."
"The fact of the matter is we had an interest rate cut about two weeks ago; it was the fourth in a series," Costello said.
The Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy on four occasions between July and May, each time dropping its target for overnight cash rates by 0.5 percentage points.
Short-term interest rates anticipate a moderate chance of a fifth 50 basis point easing in the next six months.

Australian economists usually say that monetary adjustments take 12 to 18 months to have their effect on the economy, although a round of tightenings in late 1994 are thought to have had a much faster effect.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said March quarter gross domestic product had grown 0.9 percent from the previous quarter and 2.4 percent from a year before.
